title: The matching object is the degree-n term of the (n-1)-coskeleton
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with finite limits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits], let $K$ be a simplicial object of $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] and let $n\geq1$. Let $M_n(K)$, with projections $\mathrm{pr}_i:M_n(K)\to K_{n-1}$ ($0\leq i\leq n$), and $\mu_n:K_n\to M_n(K)$ be the matching object and the matching morphism of [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-matching-object]. Then the $(n-1)$-coskeleton $L=\mathrm{cosk}_{n-1}\mathrm{sk}_{n-1}K$ of $\mathrm{sk}_{n-1}K$ exists [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton], with counit $\varepsilon:\mathrm{sk}_{n-1}L\to\mathrm{sk}_{n-1}K$ and canonical morphism $c:K\to L$, and there is a unique morphism $\theta:L_n\to M_n(K)$ with $\mathrm{pr}_i\circ\theta=\varepsilon_{n-1}\circ d^L_i$ for $0\leq i\leq n$ (where $d^L_i:L_n\to L_{n-1}$ are the face maps of $L$ and $\varepsilon_{n-1}:L_{n-1}\to K_{n-1}$ is the degree-$(n-1)$ component of $\varepsilon$); $\theta$ is an isomorphism, and $\theta\circ c_n=\mu_n$, where $c_n:K_n\to L_n$ is the degree-$n$ component of $c$.

source.place: Lemma 0183 (lemma-existence-cosk: existence of cosk_m and the formula (cosk_m U)_n = lim over (Delta/[n])_{<=m}^{opp} of U(n)) and Lemma 0186 (lemma-formula-limit: that limit, for n = m+1, represents the functor of tuples (f_0,...,f_{m+1}) with d_{j-1} f_i = d_i f_j); used in hypercovering.tex Definition 01G5 (definition-hypercovering), condition (2)

proof.text: Put $V=\mathrm{sk}_{n-1}K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-coskeleton-matching-tuples], the $(n-1)$-coskeleton $(L,\varepsilon)$ exists and, for every $W$, maps $W\to L_n$ correspond naturally to compatible families $(x_\alpha:W\to K_k)_\alpha$ indexed by all order-preserving $\alpha:[k]\to[n]$ with $k\leq n-1$; the canonical map $c_n$ corresponds to $(K(\alpha))_\alpha$.

source.place: Lemma 0183, formula for cosk_m, with m=n-1

proof.text: Restriction sends an all-$\alpha$ compatible family to its injective proper-face subfamily. Conversely, factor each proper $\alpha$ through a missing face using [lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-factorization]; independence of the missing face follows by factoring through two missing faces and applying [lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-face-identity], and compatibility follows from contravariance of $K$. Thus all-map families and injective proper-face families are naturally bijective, as in the proof of Stacks Lemma 0186.

source.place: Lemma 0186 proof, factorization through a face and independence of the factorization

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-matching-object-proper-faces] (1) and (2), injective proper-face families are represented by $M_n(K)$, with cone projections $\pi_\delta$; by its (3), the family represented by $\mu_n$ is $(K(\alpha))_\alpha$ after the extension of Step 2. Hence $L_n$ and $M_n(K)$ represent the same natural functor of all-map compatible families.

source.place: Lemma 0186 statement and proof, represented compatible families

proof.text: The unique comparison morphism $\theta:L_n\to M_n(K)$ between the two representations has the stated projection equations. The inverse comparison is obtained in the opposite direction; naturality and injectivity of the representing bijections show both composites are identities, so $\theta$ is an isomorphism. The canonical map $c_n$ and $\mu_n$ represent the same family $(K(\alpha))_\alpha$, hence $\theta\circ c_n=\mu_n$.

lean.statement: theorem matching_object_coskeleton {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasFiniteLimits C] (K : SimplicialObject C) (n : ℕ) (M : Cone (SimplicialObject.matchingBoundaryIndex K n).multicospan) (_hM : IsLimit M) (μ : K _⦋n + 2⦌ ⟶ M.pt) (_hμ : ∀ i : Fin (n + 3), μ ≫ M.π.app (WalkingMulticospan.left i) = K.δ i) : ∃ (L : SimplicialObject C) (ε : (SimplicialObject.truncation (n + 1)).obj L ⟶ (SimplicialObject.truncation (n + 1)).obj K), L.IsRightKanExtension ε ∧ ∃ (c : K ⟶ L), (SimplicialObject.truncation (n + 1)).map c ≫ ε = 𝟙 ((SimplicialObject.truncation (n + 1)).obj K) ∧ ∃ (θ : L _⦋n + 2⦌ ⟶ M.pt), (∀ i : Fin (n + 3), θ ≫ M.π.app (WalkingMulticospan.left i) = L.δ i ≫ ε.app (op ⟨SimplexCategory.mk (n + 1), Nat.le_refl (n + 1)⟩)) ∧ (∀ θ' : L _⦋n + 2⦌ ⟶ M.pt, (∀ i : Fin (n + 3), θ' ≫ M.π.app (WalkingMulticospan.left i) = L.δ i ≫ ε.app (op ⟨SimplexCategory.mk (n + 1), Nat.le_refl (n + 1)⟩)) → θ' = θ) ∧ IsIso θ ∧ c.app (op (SimplexCategory.mk (n + 2))) ≫ θ = μ
lean.note: The two declarations cover degree one and degree n+2 for every natural n. Limiting fans/cones and matching-map equations specify the matching objects of the dependency; coskeleton existence is stated using Mathlib IsRightKanExtension, without assuming a Kan-extension instance.
